header.business: Example Tea Co., a two-person online shop selling loose-leaf tea, samplers and teaware to home tea drinkers across the US

rivals.reading: Meta page 'Competitor A' (Tea room) matched; Google creatives counted, undated
Meta page 'Competitor B' (Gift shop) matched; Google creatives counted, undated
Meta: no page fits (search returned 'Competitor C Sound' (Musician/band)), so Meta is unknown; Google: no creatives on its domain

top_ten.first_test: A subscription page and checkout option for a 3-blend monthly box
top_ten.impact_basis: 4,000 monthly searches x 3% (assumption) = 120.0 visits x 2.81% Organic Search rate = 3.4 orders a month
evidence: own proof: Organic Search converts at 2.81%, above the 2.77% site rate
rival proof: 1 rival runs 'subscription' ads on Meta now; the longest has been live 141 days
top_ten.this_week: Price a 3-blend box and add a subscription option to checkout

check.keep_if: 1.7 or more orders a month (half the estimate)
check.stop_if: under 1.7 orders a month at week 12

top_ten.first_test: A page for the existing 6-blend sampler, written for sampler searches
top_ten.impact_basis: 3,900 monthly searches x 3% (assumption) = 117.0 visits x 2.81% Organic Search rate = 3.3 orders a month
evidence: own proof: Organic Search converts at 2.81%, above the 2.77% site rate
no rival proof yet: 1 rival runs 'sampler' ads on Meta now; the longest has been live 39 days (needs 60+ days or 2+ rivals)
top_ten.this_week: Publish a sampler page that names all six blends and their steeping times

check.keep_if: 1.6 or more orders a month (half the estimate)
check.stop_if: under 1.6 orders a month at week 12

top_ten.first_test: One guide page for the four infuser teapots in stock
top_ten.impact_basis: 3,600 monthly searches x 3% (assumption) = 108.0 visits x 2.81% Organic Search rate = 3.0 orders a month
evidence: own proof: Organic Search converts at 2.81%, above the 2.77% site rate
top_ten.this_week: Write the guide around the four infuser teapots in stock

check.keep_if: 1.5 or more orders a month (half the estimate)
check.stop_if: under 1.5 orders a month at week 12

top_ten.idea: Paid search test on gift-set searches
top_ten.first_test: $300 over 4 weeks on gift-set phrases, sending clicks to the gift set page
top_ten.impact_basis: $300 / $1.00 average CPC = 300.0 visits x 2.77% site rate = 8.3 orders a month
evidence: rival proof: 1 rival runs 'gift set' ads on Meta now; the longest has been live 75 days
top_ten.ease_basis: 6 hours, less 2 because $300 is over half the $500 budget = Ease 7
top_ten.this_week: Set up one search campaign with the two gift-set phrases and a $300 cap

check.keep_if: 4.2 or more orders a month (half the estimate)
check.stop_if: under 4.2 orders a month at week 4

top_ten.idea: Review request email with a photo prompt two weeks after delivery
top_ten.first_test: One automated email asking for a review and a photo of the cup
top_ten.impact_basis: judgment (the email asks for a review, not an order), capped at 5
evidence: own proof: Email converts at 6.00%, above the 2.77% site rate
top_ten.this_week: Write the review email and set it to send 14 days after delivery

top_ten.idea: 'Name our next blend' vote for the email list
top_ten.first_test: One email with a three-name vote; the winner launches next month
top_ten.impact_basis: judgment (the email asks for a vote, not an order), capped at 5
evidence: own proof: Email converts at 6.00%, above the 2.77% site rate
top_ten.this_week: Send the vote email with three names

top_ten.idea: A second monthly email: one brewing tip and one featured blend
top_ten.first_test: Two sends to the full list, a tip-led email mid-month next to the new-blend email
top_ten.impact_basis: 2,400 people x 3% clicks (assumption) x 1 send = 72.0 visits x 6.00% Email rate = 4.3 orders a month
evidence: own proof: Email converts at 6.00%, above the 2.77% site rate
top_ten.this_week: Draft the first tip email around the most-searched brewing question

check.keep_if: 2.1 or more orders a month (half the estimate)
check.stop_if: under 2.1 orders a month at week 4

top_ten.idea: Ask the three blogs that already send buyers for a spot in their holiday gift guides
top_ten.first_test: A short pitch with a sampler for each editor
evidence: own proof: Referral converts at 3.05%, above the 2.77% site rate
top_ten.this_week: Find the three referring blogs in GA4 and send each editor a sampler with a two-line pitch

top_ten.idea: Promoted Pinterest pins for the gift sets
top_ten.first_test: $200 over 4 weeks on six gift-set pins
evidence: rival proof: 1 rival runs 'gift set' ads on Meta now; the longest has been live 75 days
top_ten.this_week: Make six gift-set pins and set a $200 cap

top_ten.idea: Meta ads to a lookalike of past buyers
top_ten.first_test: $250 over 4 weeks to a 1% lookalike of past buyers, excluding current followers
evidence: rival proof: 2 rivals run 'prospecting' ads on Meta now; the longest has been live 101 days
top_ten.this_week: Build a 1% lookalike from past buyers, exclude followers, cap at $250
top_ten.note: kept although tried before: it reaches new people who look like buyers and excludes followers, which is why the boosts failed

start_with.limits: $500 and 32 hours (one month at 8 hours a week)

assumptions: A new search page reaches 3% of its phrases' monthly searches as visits
An email gets 3% clicks per send (the shop gave no click rate)
An email sent 45 days after each order reaches about one month's orders each month
Paid search visits use the site rate, because the shop has no paid search history
unknowns: Competitor C: no Meta page fit its name and trade, and no Google creatives were found on its domain, so its ad activity is unknown
Google Ads Transparency results carry no dates, format or ad text, so Google counts show presence only and add no rival proof
Competitor A has 1 Meta ad with template placeholder text, so no offer was read from it
Click rates for the shop's own emails were not given, so email estimates use the 3% assumption
